claim.why_it_matters: Sibling clauses of identical depth are emitted at two different heading levels. At level 2 these sub-clauses become outline siblings of their own parent group and of 8.3.2.3 System-names (also `##` on page 133), so the user-defined-word catalogue loses its nesting. The same split continues across pages 132-135 (8.3.2.2.13-8.3.2.2.31 and 8.3.2.3.2-8.3.2.3.12 at `##` while 8.3.2.3.1 General is `###`).

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds.

(1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claim is filed as kind=missing-heading, but every heading printed on page 131 is present in the markdown with exact clause number and exact title. Reading spec_p131.png against page-131.md line by line: 8.3.2.2.2 Class-name, .3 Compilation-variable-name, .4 Condition-name, .5 Constant-name, .6 Data-name, .7 Directive-name, .8 Dynamic-length-structure-name, .9 File-name, .10 Function-prototype-name, .11 Index-name, .12 Interface-name - all 11 headings present, all 11 body paragraphs present and textually faithful. Zero omitted content. The claim is about the `#` count only.

(2) HEADING LEVEL CARRIES NO HIERARCHY INFORMATION ANYWHERE IN THIS FILE, so page 131 is not deviating from a convention. Measured across the whole 2.9 MB transcription, the markdown level is uncorrelated with clause-number depth: 5-deep numbers appear at `##` 118 times, `###` 128 times, `####` 41 times; 4-deep at 162/620/24; 3-deep at 276/508/17; 1-deep (e.g. `8.3`) always at `##`. The claim samples one arbitrary draw from this document-wide noise (page 130's `###`), declares it the standard, and calls the equally arbitrary neighbouring draw a structural defect. Page 130 is not a baseline. The same alternation recurs at 8.3.3.4.1-.3 (`###`) vs .4 (`##`), 8.3.3.5.1-.2 (`###`) vs .3-.4 (`##`), 8.3.3.6.1 (`####`) vs .2-.3 (`##`) vs .4 (`###`) - it is conversion noise, not a page-131 event.

(3) THE CLAIMED HARM DOES NOT FOLLOW; THE PROPOSED BASELINE WOULD NOT FIX IT. The claim says level 2 makes these clauses 'outline siblings of their own parent group', implying `###` would nest them correctly. It would not. The parent 8.3.2.2 User-defined words is emitted at `####` (line 5337) - DEEPER than both the `###` 8.3.2.2.1 (line 5470) and the `##` 8.3.2.2.2 (line 5483). Grandparent 8.3.2 is `###` (line 5312); great-grandparent 8.3 is `##` (line 5302). The outline above these clauses is already fully inverted, so 8.3.2.2.1 at `###` is no more a child of its `####` parent than 8.3.2.2.2 at `##` is. Promoting page 131 to `###` would merely make it a sibling of its own grandparent. The nesting the claim says is 'lost' never existed in this file and the claim's own remedy does not restore it.

(4) NO MEANING IS AT RISK. The full hierarchy is carried explicitly and unambiguously by the dotted clause number inside the heading text ('8.3.2.2.2') and duplicated in the `<a id="section-8-3-2-2-2">` anchor. Any consumer derives depth from the number, never from the `#` count. For this project's actual use of the spec - citing an exact section/GR - the citable identity of every clause on page 131 is intact and exact.

This is presentational rendering furniture, uniform across the document, with identical content on both sides. It meets the stated rejection criteria 'the difference is only ... formatting' and 'the difference does not change meaning', and it additionally misdescribes its own kind (nothing is missing) and misstates its baseline.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-131 PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. All 11 clause headings and all body text on page 131 are transcribed completely and accurately. The only difference is the markdown heading level (`##` vs `###`), which in this transcription is uncorrelated with clause depth document-wide (5-deep clauses appear at `##`/`###`/`####` 118/128/41 times respectively) and which is contradicted by the parent chain itself - 8.3.2.2 is `####` while its children are `###` and `##`. If the unreliable heading-level mapping is worth tracking at all, it is a single global note about the conversion, not a per-page structural finding against 131 (or 132-135); no page-level edit could make it consistent without re-leveling every numbered heading in the file.
